text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Bank insurer ING buys U.S. insurer Equitable of Iowa for $2.2 billion. (p1)
- The three southern provinces of the Netherlands excede average national economic growth. (p1)
- Growing investor "mania" on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange. (p1)
- Food and detergent group Unilever wins first battle in Italian ice-cream war. (p3)
- Driverless bus seating eight people starts a year-long trial service between Rotterdam and Capelle a/d IJssel. (p3)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Truck maker DAF, owned by U.S. Paccar plans to move part of its assembling activities to England. (p2)
- Amsterdam merchant bank MeesPierson loses four specialists to U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch. (p2)
- Seed company Vanderhave closes its trial field of genetically modified corn in Germany. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Information technology Simac gains strength through its takeover of Lorje Computers. (p19)
- Dutch Computer software group Cap Gemini NV books strong growth in first half results. (p19)
- Merchant bank MeesPierson offers direct computer currency transaction for businesses and wealthy customers. (p21)
TROUW
- Dutch Rail NS' French rival CGEA, which took over Lovers Rail, has had problems in Britain. (p1)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Dispensing chemists' cooperative OPG is to speed up implementation of McKinsey's restructuring advice. (p9)
